dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Bengals Face Commanders on MNF With Joe Burrow Cleared
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: At 7-2 and leading the AFC North, Cincinnati enters Monday Night Football against Washington (3-5-1) boasting the NFL's top-ranked passing offense. Head coach Zac Taylor's squad must protect Burrow while masking run-defense vulnerabilities (#31 in YPC allowed) to maintain their 95.4% playoff projection.
bullets: Joe Burrow fully practiced after overcoming an illness and carries no game designation, as reported by [Ben Baby](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50544261/burrow-practices-again-full-strength-mnf), backed by Zac Taylor and offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher's collaborative scheme [bengals.com Official](https://www.bengals.com/news/game-within-the-game-zac-taylor-s-coaching-collaboration-justin-hill-justin-rascati-brad-kragthore-defines-bengals-hottest-offense-in-all-the-land).

Right tackle Amarius Mims remains pivotal in pass protection for Burrow, helping power an offense generating an NFL-best +10.71 passing EPA per game, per [Ben Baby](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50543897/bengals-amarius-mims-pass-protection-joe-burrow).

Defensive coordinator Al Golden's unit seeks to leverage Cincinnati's #3 red-zone defense (40% TD rate allowed) on Monday Night Football, via [bengals.com Official](https://www.bengals.com/news/game-preview-2026-week-11-bengals-comanders-monday-night-football).

On the roster front, Cincinnati placed linebacker Oren Burks on injured reserve with a groin ailment, per [Cincinnati Bengals Official](https://www.bengals.com/team/transactions/#tx-b46be06177f4), while guard Dalton Risner remains out.
